clue.text: More primitive sort of appeal in this campaigner

indicators.note: the appeal is put in the middle of the word for more primitive, so it signals one piece set inside another

parts.note: cruder means more primitive or less refined
SA is short for sex appeal, one sort of appeal

explanation.surface: A campaigner whose cause has a cruder, more basic kind of appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause.

clue.text: Serves on ship, say, for a holiday voyage

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken out loud and heard as another

parts.note: to crew is to serve on a ship

explanation.surface: Working on board a ship while on a holiday trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage taken as a holiday.

clue.text: Agree to be subject to arrest

parts.note: under means subject to, as in 'under orders'
to take a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Someone consents to being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake is to promise or commit to do something.

clue.text: A canon found about midnight stranded on the beach

indicators.note: the A and the canon are found standing round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a round is a musical canon, in which voices enter in turn singing the same tune
the middle of 'night' is the letter G

explanation.surface: A churchman found at about midnight stranded on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' looks like a clergyman, but it is the musical round. 'about' wraps A ROUND around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship aground has run onto the shore or seabed and is stuck.

clue.text: Oriental man's basis for living and thinking

parts.note: E, East, stands for Oriental
Thos is the written short form of Thomas, a man's name, with the 's supplying the final letter

explanation.surface: An Eastern man's philosophy of life.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the guiding character or set of beliefs of a person or community.

clue.text: Wages withheld in retribution

parts.note: wages are pay
something withheld or cancelled is off, as in 'the deal is off'

explanation.surface: Docking someone's wages as a form of punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A payoff can be a final reckoning or comeuppance, the punishment someone eventually gets.

clue.text: Name for mean man staggering around Indian city?

indicators.note: the jumbled man goes around the city, enclosing it
the letters of man stagger into a new order

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: A nickname for a stingy man reeling round an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself cryptic: the four letters of 'name' rearrange to 'mean', so the answer is literally a name for 'mean'. 'staggering' scrambles the man; 'around' wraps him round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of mean gives name, and a word formed by such rearranging is the device in question.

clue.text: Mac's expression of surprise concerning natural earth

parts.note: och is a Scottish exclamation; Mac stands for a Scot
re means concerning

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims in surprise about something in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a natural earth pigment, yellow to brownish red.

clue.text: They transfer their charges from one bank to another

definitions.text: They transfer their charges from one bank to another

parts.words: They transfer their charges from one bank to another
parts.note: reads as financiers moving fees between banks, but means boatmen taking passengers from one riverbank to the opposite one

explanation.definitionFit: Ferry operators carry passengers, their charges, across a river between its banks.

clue.text: He does porridge if caught? He does

definitions.text: He does porridge if caught? He does

parts.words: He does porridge if caught? He does
parts.note: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, and to do someone is to cheat them, so this is a cheat who serves time when caught

explanation.definitionFit: A con man cheats people and goes to prison if he is caught.

clue.text: He turned out garments to clothe the sick

indicators.note: the letters of 'He turned' are turned out, set out in a new order
the clothing word wraps itself around 'the', putting it inside

parts.note: clothing is wear, as in menswear
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charitable man who made clothes for the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like the clue's subject, but 'He turned' is the fodder that 'out' rearranges; 'to clothe' is the container signal, not a charity's mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling under the weather is an idiom for being unwell or slightly ill.

clue.text: Conceals ropes on board

explanation.surface: Something hides the rigging on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To shroud is to cover or hide; shrouds are also the ropes supporting a ship's mast.

clue.text: Sort of slopes where plants are cultivated?

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of hillsides plants are grown on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery slopes are the gentle ski runs for beginners; a nursery is also a place raising young plants for sale.

clue.text: Publicity for labourer appearing before beak

indicators.note: the worker's word comes first, ahead of the beak's word, in the answer

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: A worker getting press attention when they appear before a magistrate (a beak, in British slang).
explanation.definitionFit: A handbill is a printed advertising leaflet handed out to passers-by.

clue.text: Soldiers assembled in attempt to detain agitator

indicators.note: the attempt phrase holds the agitator inside, detaining it

parts.note: taken as written
an attempt is a try
a fan agitates, or stirs up, the air

explanation.surface: Troops gathered to try to hold a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers collectively.

clue.text: Tree identified by a Christie heroine right away

indicators.note: the right letter is sent away, taken out of the sleuth's name

parts.note: Miss Marple is Agatha Christie's elderly detective

explanation.surface: A tree pinpointed at once by one of Agatha Christie's detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a tree, source of syrup and the leaf on Canada's flag.

clue.text: Carrier's charge in the days of "Kiss me, Kate'?

parts.note: Kiss Me, Kate is the musical by Cole Porter
an age is a span of days, an era

explanation.surface: What a delivery firm charged in the era of a classic musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter wrote the musical, so its 'days' are the Porter age; the composer's name comes first in the answer although the clue puts the days first.
explanation.definitionFit: Porterage is the fee paid for carrying goods or luggage.

clue.text: Bulletin reveals Surrey opener among substitute players

indicators.note: the opening letter is placed among the letters of the players phrase

parts.note: a replacement group of actors is a new cast

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: News reports that a Surrey opening batsman is among the replacement players.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county with a famous cricket team, so 'opener' suggests a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast news bulletin.

clue.text: Archdeacon joins opponents, possibly winning an identical amount

indicators.note: the churchman joins the pair of opponents by sitting between them

parts.note: E and S, East and South, are opposing partnerships at the bridge table
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A churchman sits down with rivals at cards, perhaps hoping to come out even.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and South are on opposite sides, so they are 'opponents'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds of evens mean a winning bet returns exactly the stake again.

clue.text: Russian vessel taking American uncle and soldiers round state

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

indicators.note: the soldiers go round the state, enclosing it

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: A Russian ship carries Uncle Sam and troops around a state.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian metal urn for boiling water for tea.

clue.text: Tip off regarding hostilities in Egyptian borders

parts.note: for can mean regarding, as in 'so much for that'

indicators.note: the fighting word sits inside the frame made by the Egyptian's outer letters
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: hostilities are war

explanation.surface: A warning given about fighting on Egypt's frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes E and N, the first and last letters of 'Egyptian'; 'in' puts WAR between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To forewarn someone is to give them advance notice, which is what a tip-off does.

clue.text: Feeble sound with which the world ends, Eliot thought

definitions.text: with which the world ends, Eliot thought

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot's view that the world ends quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimper is a weak cry; Eliot's The Hollow Men closes 'not with a bang but a whimper'.

clue.text: Coming to old Roman passage

parts.note: ad is the Latin word for to
a vent is an outlet or passage for air

explanation.surface: Arriving at an ancient Roman corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival, the coming of something.

clue.text: Island novelist initially sent Hansel and Gretel to sleep

definitions.text: sent Hansel and Gretel to sleep

indicators.note: the novelist's name is placed first, before the island, despite the clue's order

parts.note: George Sand was a French novelist
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A novelist from an island first sent Hansel and Gretel to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: In Humperdinck's opera Hansel and Gretel, the Sandman sprinkles sand to send the children to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandman is the folklore figure who brings sleep to children, appearing in the opera.

clue.text: Material sported by many long-legged women

indicators.note: the fabric is worn by the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A fabric worn by lots of leggy women.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic material, famously used for stockings.

clue.text: A requisite one's incorporated in cake flavouring

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the one's letters are taken into the body of the requisite word

parts.note: a requisite is a need
one's reads as 'one is': I for one, then the 's supplies S

explanation.surface: A recipe ingredient that must be added to a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed, the seed of the anise plant, gives a liquorice taste to cakes and sweets.

clue.text: A measure of acidity is a pest in the garden

parts.note: taken as written
pH is the scale measuring acidity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soil acidity is a garden nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphis is an aphid, a greenfly sapping garden plants.

clue.text: Completely finished the soft fabric, being in total chaos

parts.note: all over means completely finished, as in 'it's all over'
taken as written
p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off the soft material and the result is a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the place is an idiom for disorganised and scattered everywhere.

clue.text: Doctor swallowed by big fish in Arctic terrain

indicators.note: the doctor is swallowed, so goes inside the fish's name

parts.note: the tuna is a large ocean fish

explanation.surface: A doctor eaten by a huge fish in the frozen north.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the treeless, frozen plain of the Arctic regions.

clue.text: Reunites characters like Bunter.

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the clue's first word are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A reunion of characters in the style of Billy Bunter's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the famously greedy fat schoolboy of Frank Richards' Greyfriars stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient means greedy or hungry, the defining trait of the gluttonous schoolboy.
